concepts.name: Equilibrium Price and Quantity: Definition and Determination
key_dimensions: How equilibrium is reached through intersection of demand and supply curves
Distinction between equilibrium price vs. market-clearing price (often confused as different)
Why equilibrium is a tendency, not a guaranteed real-world state
Difference between static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium

concepts.name: Excess Demand (Shortage) and Its Market Adjustment Mechanism
key_dimensions: Conditions under which excess demand arises (price below equilibrium)
Price signaling mechanism that eliminates shortage in free markets
Why shortages persist in controlled/regulated markets (price ceilings)
Real-world examples: Essential commodity shortages, fuel crises

concepts.name: Excess Supply (Surplus) and Its Market Adjustment Mechanism
key_dimensions: Conditions under which excess supply arises (price above equilibrium)
Downward price pressure and inventory accumulation as adjustment signals
Why surpluses persist under price floors (e.g., MSP in agricultural markets)
Government procurement as a surplus-absorption mechanism in India

concepts.name: Shifts in Equilibrium: Demand-Side vs. Supply-Side Changes
key_dimensions: Distinguishing movement along a curve vs. shift of the curve (common UPSC trap)
Effect of simultaneous shifts in both demand and supply on equilibrium price and quantity
Indeterminate outcomes when both curves shift (e.g., price indeterminate if both demand and supply increase)
Real-world triggers: Income changes, input cost changes, technology shocks

concepts.name: Stable vs. Unstable Equilibrium in Markets
key_dimensions: Walrasian stability: Price adjusts to restore equilibrium after disturbance
Marshallian stability: Quantity adjusts to restore equilibrium
Conditions under which equilibrium is unstable (upward-sloping demand or downward-sloping supply)
Cobweb model as a classic example of oscillating/unstable equilibrium (agricultural markets)

concepts.name: Price Ceiling (Maximum Price) and Its Effects on Market Equilibrium
key_dimensions: Binding vs. non-binding price ceiling distinction (ceiling below equilibrium = binding)
Consequences: Shortages, black markets, quality deterioration, rationing
Indian context: Essential Commodities Act, rent control, drug price caps (DPCO)
Welfare analysis: Consumer surplus gain vs. deadweight loss

concepts.name: Price Floor (Minimum Price) and Its Effects on Market Equilibrium
key_dimensions: Binding vs. non-binding price floor (floor above equilibrium = binding)
Consequences: Surplus, government procurement burden, storage costs
Indian context: MSP as a price floor and its debate on being legally binding
Minimum wage as a price floor in labour markets — employment effects

concepts.name: Consumer Surplus and Producer Surplus at Equilibrium
key_dimensions: Geometric interpretation of surplus areas under/above equilibrium price
How price changes redistribute surplus between consumers and producers
Total social welfare = Consumer Surplus + Producer Surplus (at competitive equilibrium)
Deadweight loss as reduction in total surplus due to market distortions

concepts.name: Deadweight Loss: Causes and Policy Implications
key_dimensions: How taxes, subsidies, price controls, and monopoly create deadweight loss
Graphical area of deadweight loss triangle and its economic meaning
Difference: Deadweight loss from tax vs. deadweight loss from price ceiling (often confused)
Minimizing deadweight loss — Ramsey pricing principle, tax on inelastic goods

concepts.name: Equilibrium in Competitive Markets vs. Monopoly Markets
key_dimensions: Competitive equilibrium: P = MC = MR (efficient outcome)
Monopoly equilibrium: P > MC, output below competitive level
Sources of welfare loss under monopoly compared to competitive equilibrium
Natural monopoly equilibrium and regulatory pricing (Average Cost Pricing vs. Marginal Cost Pricing)

concepts.name: General Equilibrium vs. Partial Equilibrium Analysis
key_dimensions: Partial equilibrium: Analyzing one market in isolation (ceteris paribus assumption)
General equilibrium: Simultaneous equilibrium across all interconnected markets (Walras's Law)
When partial equilibrium analysis is misleading (spillover effects, input-output linkages)
Policy relevance: Why a tax in one sector can disturb equilibrium in unrelated sectors

concepts.name: Market Equilibrium Under Different Market Structures
key_dimensions: Perfect competition: P = MC, zero economic profit in long run
Monopolistic competition: P > MC, excess capacity in equilibrium
Oligopoly: Nash equilibrium concept, interdependence of firms
Comparison of output and price levels across structures — key UPSC ranking question

concepts.name: Effect of Taxes and Subsidies on Market Equilibrium
key_dimensions: Tax incidence: How the burden splits between buyers and sellers based on elasticity
Specific tax vs. ad valorem tax — different effects on equilibrium
Subsidy as negative tax — effect on equilibrium price, quantity, and government expenditure
Elasticity rule: More inelastic side bears greater tax burden (common UPSC trap)

concepts.name: Elasticity and Its Role in Determining Equilibrium Outcomes
key_dimensions: How price elasticity of demand and supply determines magnitude of price and quantity changes after a shift
Perfectly inelastic supply: Entire price change borne by consumers (e.g., land market)
Perfectly elastic supply: Entire adjustment through quantity, price unchanged
Agricultural market instability: Inelastic demand + supply shocks = large price swings

concepts.name: Labour Market Equilibrium: Wages, Employment, and Distortions
key_dimensions: Equilibrium wage determined by intersection of labour demand (MRP) and labour supply
Minimum wage above equilibrium creating unemployment (price floor analogy)
Monopsony in labour market: Wage below competitive equilibrium, under-employment
India-specific: Informal labour markets, wage rigidity, and non-clearing labour markets

concepts.name: Cobweb Model and Lagged Supply Adjustment in Agricultural Markets
key_dimensions: Why agricultural markets show cyclical price fluctuations (supply lags due to production cycle)
Convergent, divergent, and continuous cobweb depending on relative elasticities
Convergent cobweb: Supply more elastic than demand — prices stabilize over time
Policy implication: Price stabilization funds, futures markets to break cobweb cycles

concepts.name: Equilibrium with Externalities: Market Failure and Correction
key_dimensions: Negative externality: Private equilibrium overproduces compared to social optimum (MSC > MPC)
Positive externality: Private equilibrium underproduces compared to social optimum
Pigouvian tax/subsidy to restore socially optimal equilibrium
Coase Theorem: Private bargaining can reach social optimum without government intervention (under zero transaction costs)

concepts.name: Equilibrium in Money Market: LM Curve and Interest Rate Determination
key_dimensions: Money market equilibrium: Money supply = Money demand (liquidity preference)
How RBI's open market operations shift money supply and change equilibrium interest rate
Liquidity trap: Money demand becomes perfectly elastic, monetary policy ineffective
IS-LM framework: Simultaneous equilibrium in goods market and money market

concepts.name: Nash Equilibrium in Oligopolistic Markets
key_dimensions: Nash equilibrium definition: No player benefits by unilaterally changing strategy
Prisoner's Dilemma as Nash equilibrium that is not Pareto optimal
Cournot equilibrium (quantity competition) vs. Bertrand equilibrium (price competition) — different Nash outcomes
Cartel instability: Why Nash equilibrium leads to defection from cooperative agreement (OPEC context)

concepts.name: Walras's Law and Aggregate Market Equilibrium
key_dimensions: Walras's Law: If n-1 markets are in equilibrium, the nth market must also be in equilibrium
Implication: Excess demand in one market must equal excess supply in another
Distinction between Walras's Law and Say's Law (common confusion in UPSC prep)
Limitation: Applies to exchange economies; breaks down with money, expectations, and price rigidities
